```{r}
#| label: setup-triangulation
#| include: false
root <- Sys.getenv("TRI_REPO_ROOT")
run_dir <- Sys.getenv("TRI_RUN_DIR")
output <- Sys.getenv("TRI_OUTPUT_DIR")
if (!nzchar(root) || !dir.exists(run_dir) || !dir.exists(output)) {
  stop("Use the dedicated triangulation Make targets from the repository root.")
}
source(file.path(root, "R", "bmi_hypercapnia_triangulation.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "triangulation_reporting.R"))
require_tri_packages(c("ggplot2", "jsonlite", "digest", "knitr"))
bundle <- read_tri_bundle(run_dir)
analysis <- bundle$analysis
results <- analysis$results
artificial <- bundle$manifest$mode == "fixture"
figures <- tri_figure_candidates(results, artificial)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "png")
pretty_count <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
frame_label <- function(x) unname(triangulation_frames[x])
outcome_label <- function(x) unname(triangulation_outcomes[x])
table_out <- function(x, caption, ...) knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, ...)
```

```{r}
#| label: status-banner
#| results: asis
cat(if (artificial) "**ARTIFICIAL FIXTURE — workflow and layout validation only. Every numerical result below is simulated and is not a study finding.**\n\n" else "**DRAFT CLINICAL RENDER — input-manifest checks passed; scientific qualification, coauthor review, and release remain separate.**\n\n")
```

# Question and fixed specification

What fraction of modeled hypercapnia frequency is associated with BMI above 40 across the prespecified grid? The primary quantity is the **potential impact fraction under a scenario setting BMI above 40 to 40 kg/m²**; BMI at or below 40 is unchanged. Both scenarios average predictions over the same model-evaluable patients, with original frames, indexes, and adjustment variables fixed. No patient is removed because their hypothetical BMI crosses the sampling-frame boundary.

For each cell, the fraction is $1 - \bar p_{\mathrm{BMI\ to\ 40}} / \bar p_{\mathrm{observed\ BMI}}$. We also report the two probabilities and their absolute difference. These are association-based, model-standardized contrasts for documented hypercapnia at the selected encounter. They do not establish a reduction in new-case incidence or a treatment effect.

The source is restricted to adults aged at least 18 with emergency or inpatient encounters starting in **2022**. Each sampling frame selects each original patient's **first qualifying encounter**, before considering outcome availability or completeness of the adjustment variables. A patient can have different index encounters across frames. The legacy derived BMI is used unchanged.

| Sampling frame | Membership at the selected encounter |
|:--|:--|
| Severe obesity | BMI ≥40 kg/m² |
| ABG obtained | Arterial gas drawn; no BMI threshold |
| Either gas obtained | Arterial or venous gas drawn; no BMI threshold |

The three outcomes are the legacy ICD composite (J96.02/J96.12/J96.22/J96.92/E66.2), arterial PaCO$_2$ ≥45 mm Hg, and arterial PaCO$_2$ ≥45 **or** venous PCO$_2$ ≥50 mm Hg. Neither pH nor ventilatory support is required. The ICD composite includes an obesity-specific diagnosis; no exclusion sensitivity is performed.

For the combined gas outcome, any qualifying measured result establishes positivity. At least one valid measured gas, with no available result reaching its threshold, establishes an **available-gas negative**. No usable gases remains unknown. An available-gas negative does not establish what an unmeasured specimen would have shown.

# Cohort and index audit

```{r}
#| label: scope-counts
scope_table <- data.frame(
  Step = c("Input encounter rows", "Exact duplicates removed", "Distinct encounter versions", "Keys with conflicting versions", "In 2022 adult ED/inpatient scope", "Outside scope", "Uncertain scope"),
  N = pretty_count(unlist(analysis$scope, use.names = FALSE))
)
table_out(scope_table, "Source-scope audit. Uncertain scope is not coded as out of scope.")
```

```{r}
#| label: frame-counts
f <- analysis$frame_counts
frame_table <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(f$frame), Confirmed = pretty_count(f$n_frame_patients),
  Resolved = pretty_count(f$n_index_resolved), Unresolved = pretty_count(f$n_index_unresolved),
  `Uncertain membership only` = pretty_count(f$n_membership_uncertain), check.names = FALSE)
table_out(frame_table, "Unique patients within each frame. Frames overlap and must not be summed.")
```

“Confirmed” means at least one encounter is known to meet the sampling frame and study scope. “Unresolved” means conflicting source versions, an earliest-date tie, or an earlier potentially qualifying encounter prevents a unique index. Conflicting versions establish frame membership only when all versions agree on eligibility; they never provide resolved index values. “Uncertain membership only” means no qualifying encounter is confirmed, but membership cannot be excluded. Unresolved indexes remain counted and are excluded from models; no later encounter is substituted.

# Model and estimation checks

Each of the nine cells uses logistic regression with the same adjustment set:

```r
outcome ~ bmi + age_at_encounter +
  factor(sex) + factor(race_ethnicity) + factor(location)
```

BMI and age are linear on the log-odds scale. Each fitted model predicts the same patients twice: with observed BMI and with BMI above 40 replaced by 40. The report checks outcome/BMI variation, model-matrix rank, complete and quasi-complete separation, convergence, warnings, and finite estimates. A failed cell receives a reason and no plotted estimate. No adjustment terms or patients are silently substituted.

Potential-impact-fraction confidence limits use the delta method for the log ratio of the two mean predicted probabilities, with the full fitted coefficient covariance, then transform back to the fraction scale. These model-based 95% intervals condition on the empirical covariate distribution. They exclude uncertainty from unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and model misspecification. Negative fractions and intervals are retained. Adjusted BMI odds ratios with 95% Wald intervals remain supporting results.

# Nine-cell denominator accounting

```{r}
#| label: outcome-coverage
coverage <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  Indexed = results$n_index_resolved, Known = results$n_outcome_known,
  Missing = results$n_outcome_missing, check.names = FALSE)
table_out(coverage, "Outcome ascertainment at the selected indexes: indexed = known + missing.")
```

```{r}
#| label: model-denominators
denominators <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  Known = results$n_outcome_known, `Missing covariates` = results$n_missing_adjustment,
  Model = results$n_model, Events = results$n_events, check.names = FALSE)
table_out(denominators, "Model cases: known outcome = model cases + missing adjustment variables. Events are among model cases.")
```

Complete cases require BMI, age, sex, combined race/ethnicity, encounter location, and the selected outcome. Documented source categories are retained; missing covariates are not assigned an invented category. Drawing a gas without a usable result does not remove a patient from the gas sampling frame, but may leave that outcome unclassifiable.

# Standardized probabilities and fractions

```{r}
#| label: impact-estimates
impact_estimates <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  `PIF % (95% CI)` = ifelse(results$impact_status == "estimated", sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100 * results$impact_fraction, 100 * results$impact_conf_low, 100 * results$impact_conf_high), "Not estimable"),
  N = results$n_model, check.names = FALSE)
table_out(impact_estimates, "BMI-to-40 potential impact fractions. Intervals condition on the observed covariate distribution.")
```

```{r}
#| label: standardized-probabilities
probabilities <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  `Observed BMI %` = sprintf("%.2f", 100 * results$p_observed),
  `BMI to 40 %` = sprintf("%.2f", 100 * results$p_counterfactual),
  `Difference, pp` = sprintf("%.2f", 100 * results$absolute_difference), check.names = FALSE)
table_out(probabilities, "Mean predicted probabilities under each scenario; pp = percentage points. Same patients and denominators in both columns.")
```

```{r}
#| label: estimation-status
#| results: asis
failed <- results[results$impact_status != "estimated", ]
if (nrow(failed)) {
  print(table_out(data.frame(Frame = frame_label(failed$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(failed$outcome), Reason = failed$impact_reason), "Cells without a reportable impact fraction."))
} else {
  cat("All nine cells passed the implemented model and standardization checks. This is an engineering check, not clinical qualification.\n")
}
```

The primary fraction is a ratio of two mean probabilities; it is not an odds-ratio conversion or the average of patient-specific fractional changes. A positive fraction denotes lower modeled frequency under this BMI scenario. A negative fraction denotes higher modeled frequency. No-change scenarios have an exact zero fraction. The full-precision aggregate CSV supplies every numerical table and plot.

# Supporting associations and exposure support

```{r}
#| label: model-estimates
estimates <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  `OR (95% CI)` = ifelse(results$status == "estimated", sprintf("%.3f (%.3f–%.3f)", results$odds_ratio, results$conf_low, results$conf_high), "Not estimable"),
  N = results$n_model, check.names = FALSE)
table_out(estimates, "Supporting adjusted odds ratios per 1 kg/m² higher BMI; these are not attributable fractions.")
```

```{r}
#| label: counterfactual-support
support <- data.frame(Frame = frame_label(results$frame), Outcome = outcome_label(results$outcome),
  `BMI changed, n` = results$n_bmi_shifted,
  `Outside BMI range, n` = results$n_counterfactual_outside_support,
  `Outside, %` = ifelse(is.na(results$n_counterfactual_outside_support) | results$n_model == 0, "Not assessed", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * results$n_counterfactual_outside_support / results$n_model)), check.names = FALSE)
table_out(support, "Counterfactual exposure support within each fitted cell. Outside-range counts flag extrapolation; zero does not establish covariate-specific causal positivity.")
```

Setting BMI to 40 retains patients selected in the severe-obesity frame, including those whose observed BMI exceeded 40. In both gas-tested frames, patients with BMI ≤40 remain unchanged. The same scenario therefore estimates burden above 40 in different observed populations. If a fitted cell has no BMI as low as 40, predictions at 40 extrapolate beyond its observed BMI range; the table makes this visible.

# Interpretation and limits

Compare the magnitude and precision of the BMI-to-40 fractions across the prespecified grid, alongside their standardized probabilities and cell denominators. The analyses share patients and may select different encounters for the same patient. Their estimates are correlated. They are not independent replications; the report performs no pooling, vote count of significant findings, interaction tests, or joint specification-curve inference.

The source cohort is enriched for suspected hypercapnia, and gas testing is clinically selected. Restricting the source to 2022 adult ED/inpatient encounters does not create a representative sample of all acute-care patients. Differences between cells can reflect selection, diagnostic ascertainment, outcome frequency, BMI distributions, and missingness. Fractions standardized to measured-outcome, covariate-complete patients do not automatically describe everyone eligible for a frame. Differences do not by themselves establish causal effect modification.

A causal interpretation would require a well-defined BMI intervention, correct temporal ordering, adequate confounding control, exposure support, valid measurement, and appropriate selection/missingness assumptions. Reverse causation and clinically selected gas testing are unresolved. The inherited adjustment set is not proof of exchangeability. Calling the calculation descriptive does not satisfy these assumptions.

The legacy ICD composite includes E66.2, which incorporates obesity into the diagnosis. Gas outcomes describe recorded measurements at the selected encounter. Unknown evidence is reported separately and cannot establish clinical absence. Linearity on the log-odds scale is imposed for this first implementation; additional functional-form analyses require a separately documented extension.

# Reproducibility and qualification

The dedicated launcher estimates once and freezes an aggregate-only bundle with source/input hashes, denominator audits and the installed R environment. HTML, PDF and all figure alternatives consume that bundle. Review rerenders validate bundle hashes and do not open clinical inputs or fit models. Clinical mode also requires an explicit input and reviewed manifest matching its SHA-256, field mapping, source coding, encounter attribution, and units. These checks authenticate declared inputs; they do not independently establish scientific validity or release approval.

Only aggregate counts and model results are exported. Patient indexes and identifiers stay in memory. Local receipts, report outputs, and figures remain ignored by Git. The supplied manifest template is incomplete by design and is rejected until a data steward supplies the missing source evidence.

Existing R and Stata impact-fraction analyses remain separate. The current scenario concerns BMI above 40, not all obesity. It is a potential impact fraction under an explicit hypothetical BMI distribution; the calculation alone does not establish an intervention benefit or a GLP-1 treatment effect.
